Customer ticket:
Hi there, I’m reaching out before I place a bulk order for our new outdoor equipment line. We’re a small business, so I want to make sure I fully understand your current policies regarding product condition and pricing adjustments. Specifically, I’d like to clarify the rules around items that arrive with minor cosmetic imperfections. I’ve heard that if a bike or piece of camping gear has slight scratches or small dents, you offer a 15% discount on that specific item. Could you confirm if this is still the case? Also, I need to know the validity window for this offer. Is the 15% discount valid for 30 days from the date of purchase, or is it tied to the shipping date? I want to ensure we can accurately budget for potential returns or exchanges without any surprises. Since we’re planning to order several units next week, having this clarity upfront will help us manage our inventory and customer expectations better. Thanks for your help!

Reference standard — key facts a correct reply must convey:
- Minor damage earns a 15% discount valid for 30 days.

Handbook sections that cover this answer:
### damaged_items
# Damaged Items

1. You must report any visible damage to your Northwind Outdoor order within 48 hours of delivery. To initiate a claim, log into your account and select the "Report Damage" option. You are required to upload at least 3 high-resolution photos showing the specific defect, the overall item, and the shipping packaging. Failure to provide this visual evidence within the 48-hour window will result in an automatic denial of the claim, as we cannot verify the condition of the item after it has been used or stored.

2. If the damage is minor, such as a small scratch on a bike frame or a loose stitching on a tent fly, we will offer a 15% discount on your next purchase as a goodwill gesture. This discount is applied automatically to your account and is valid for 30 days. For major structural failures, such as a cracked wheel rim or a torn tent pole, we will issue a full refund of the item’s price, up to a maximum of $500.00 per item. Items exceeding this value require a manual review by our senior support team, which may take up to 5 business days to process.

3. When we approve a full refund or replacement, you must ship the damaged item back to our warehouse within 10 days of receiving the return authorization label. We will provide a prepaid shipping label for items under 20 lbs. For heavier items, such as mountain bikes or large camping stoves, you must arrange your own freight pickup. We will reimburse up to 50% of the shipping cost, capped at $75.00, provided you submit the original receipt within 14 days of the pickup date.

4. If the damage is caused by improper use, such as overloading a bike rack beyond its 150 lb capacity limit or using a camping stove in a non-ventilated area, the claim will be denied. We reserve the right to inspect the item upon return. If our inspection reveals signs of misuse or neglect, we will notify you within 3 business days. In such cases, you will be responsible for the return shipping costs, which typically range from $15.00 to $40.00 depending on the item’s weight and dimensions.

5. For items that are partially damaged but still functional, we may offer a repair service at no cost to you. This includes replacing broken zippers on backpacks or fixing bent handlebars on bikes. The repair process takes approximately 7 to 10 business days. During this time, you may request a loaner item if available, subject to a $20.00 deposit that is refunded upon the return of the loaner in good condition.

## Key facts

- You have 48 hours to report damage with 3 photos.
- Minor damage earns a 15% discount valid for 30 days.
- Full refunds are capped at $500.00 per item.
- You must return damaged items within 10 days.
- Misuse claims are denied, and you pay return shipping.

Assistant reply to grade:
Based on the handbook excerpts provided, I must clarify a misunderstanding in your question regarding the "15% discount on that specific item."

The handbook does **not** state that a 15% discount is applied to the specific damaged item at the time of purchase or as a price adjustment for the item itself. Instead, the policy for **minor damage** (such as small scratches or loose stitching) is as follows:

*   **Compensation Type:** You will receive a **15% discount on your *next* purchase** as a goodwill gesture. It is not a refund or discount on the current damaged item. [damaged_items]
*   **Validity Window:** This discount is valid for **30 days**. [damaged_items]
*   **Application:** The discount is applied automatically to your account. [damaged_items]

Regarding your specific question about whether the 30-day window is tied to the "date of purchase" or "shipping date" of the *damaged* item: The handbook states the discount is valid for 30 days but **does not specify** the exact start date (e.g., whether it starts from the date of the damage report, the date of approval, or the date of the original purchase). It only states that the discount is "valid for 30 days" and is "applied automatically to your account." [damaged_items]

**Important Note for Your Bulk Order:**
The handbook excerpts provided do not contain any information regarding **bulk order policies**, **business account pricing**, or **pre-purchase condition guarantees**. The "Damaged Items" section applies to claims made *after* delivery of a standard order. Since you are asking about policies for a new bulk order you have not yet placed, and the handbook does not cover bulk purchasing terms or pre-emptive pricing adjustments for cosmetic imperfections, I cannot confirm if different terms apply to your specific business scenario.

I recommend escalating this ticket to a human agent who can review your specific bulk order requirements and clarify the exact start date for the 30-day validity period of the goodwill discount.

schema.description: The reference-aware grader's verdict for one answer trace.

did_not_answer.description: true if the reply does not answer the customer's actual question
did_not_answer.title: Did Not Answer

missing_points.description: key facts from the reference standard that are omitted or stated inaccurately
missing_points.title: Missing Points

note.description: ONE short sentence describing the single most important problem (the open-coding note)
note.title: Note

pass.description: true only if every key fact is stated, every claim is supported, nothing is over-promised and the question is answered
pass.title: Pass

unsupported_claims.description: claims in the reply the handbook sections do not support
unsupported_claims.title: Unsupported Claims

wrong_tone_or_promise.description: true if the reply promises/implies something the handbook does not allow
wrong_tone_or_promise.title: Wrong Tone Or Promise
